us4_policing.topic: Policing and police violence: US and Israel

claims.text: In June 2018, 17,541 state and local agencies performed law enforcement functions in the United States, with about 1.214 million sworn and civilian personnel.

Mapping Police Violence counted 1,383 people killed by US police in 2024 and 1,314 (preliminary) in 2025, a 5% fall and the first year-over-year decline since 2019; the rate hovered around 0.345 per 100,000 from 2013 to 2020 and rose after 2021.

In 2025 Black people were killed by police at 0.75 per 100,000 (300 of 40m) and white people at 0.29 (560 of 193m), 2.6 times; about 22% of those killed were unarmed; officers were charged in 15 incidents so far in 2025; the share charged rose from about 2% to closer to 4% between 2019 and 2023.

Orr Commission findings released 1 Sep 2003: 13 Palestinians living in Israel were killed by police in October 2000 protests; police commanders made 'errors of judgment', used live rounds, rubber bullets and tear gas, showed 'prior hostility'; some acts stemmed from prejudice against Arabs; recommended dismissals and barring Shlomo Ben Ami from public security posts; findings not legally binding.
Mahash (Justice Ministry Police Investigation Unit) decided in September 2005 not to issue an indictment in any of the 13 killings by police in October 2000.

Eyad al-Hallaq, 32, autistic, was shot dead by a Border Police officer in Jerusalem's Old City on 30 May 2020; charged with reckless manslaughter June 2021; acquitted by the Jerusalem District Court on 6 July 2023 as a 'tragic mistake' in self-defence; the police internal investigations unit said he had defied instructions to stop shooting.

us4_prisons.topic: Incarceration over time, plea bargains, death penalty, prison conditions

claims.text: Ofer, the last IDF-run incarceration facility for Palestinians, was transferred to the Israel Prison Service on 3 October 2006; the Ketziot handover was 'part of a national policy of relieving the army of all its prisons'.

Times of Israel, 18 Dec 2023: about 19,372 prisoners, up over 3,000 since October; legal maximum 14,500; about 3,000 sleeping on mattresses; 84% of security prisoners in under 3 sq m each; IPS: 'We are very close to using up all the places for prisoners.'
Pew: in FY2022, of 71,954 federal defendants, 89.5% pleaded guilty, 8.2% had cases dismissed, 1.9% were convicted at trial and 290 (0.4%) acquitted.

A study by the Supreme Court's Research Center and Haifa University (reported May 2012) found over 85% of criminal cases in Israel's courts ended in a plea bargain (76.5% magistrates', 85.7% district) and 0.3% in full acquittal.
Guetzkow (2,012 Israeli cases, 2010–2011) concluded plea-bargaining in Israel in that period 'was marked by the miscarriage of justice'.
DPIC: 47 US executions in 2025, highest in fifteen years, in 11 states; Florida 19; 23 new death sentences; support 52%, lowest in fifty years (Gallup).

DPIC fact sheet 14 May 2026: executions 98 (1999), 85 (2000), 46 (2010), 28 (2015), 17 (2020), 25 (2024), 47 (2025), 12 in 2026 to 14 May; death row 2,024 on 1 Oct 2025; 27 death-penalty states and 23 without; moratoria in CA, OH, OR, PA; death sentences peaked at 325 in 1986; 202 exonerated from death row since 1973; federal 16 executions since 1977, 3 on federal death row.

Knesset passed death penalty law 30 March 2026, 62–48: hanging default for West Bank Palestinians convicted in military courts of nationalistic killings, life only in 'special circumstances'; civilian courts may choose death or life; no unanimity required; no clemency; not retroactive; Netanyahu voted for it; ACRI petitioned the High Court calling it 'discriminatory by design'; Australia, Britain, France, Germany, Italy urged dropping it; Israel's last execution was Eichmann in 1962.

Petitions by ACRI and Adalah (30 Mar 2026) and others; High Court ordered the state to respond to interim-order requests 31 Mar 2026; Central Command commander signed an order applying the law 17 May 2026; sentences must be carried out within 90 days; no ruling or death sentence reported on the page as of its latest dated item (May 2026).

PHRI (CBS/AP 17 Nov 2025): at least 94 Palestinians died in Israeli custody 7 Oct 2023–Aug 2025 (68 from Gaza, 26 West Bank), 29 at Sde Teiman; fewer than 30 in the previous ten years; post-mortems showed signs of beatings; IPS says it operates under law and oversight; IDF says detainees get three meals and medical checks; Ben-Gvir said prisons would no longer be 'summer camps'; in September 2025 the Supreme Court ordered more and better food.

us4_detention.topic: Administrative detention, military courts, children, Guantanamo, ICE

claims.text: HaMoked (from IPS data): as of October 2026 Israel holds 7,846 'security' inmates (1,509 sentenced, 3,236 remand, 3,101 administrative detainees) plus 1,419 'unlawful combatants', 9,265 in all; in June 2020: 2,834 sentenced, 1,162 remand, 356 administrative detainees, 300 unlawful combatants.

Emergency Powers (Detention) Law 1979: Defence Minister orders up to six months; detainee before District Court President within 48 hours; review every three months; applies only during a declared state of emergency, in force since the state's establishment; draws on Mandatory statutes. Military Order 1651: commanders may detain up to six months, renewable with no maximum; military judge review within eight days (at the time); most evidence not disclosed to detainee or lawyer.

Military Order 1651: minimum age of criminal responsibility 12; 12–13 max six months custody; 16+ sentenced as adults; military juvenile court set up September 2009; Order 1685 (2012) cut time before judicial review from eight to four days; 500–700 children prosecuted a year; B'Tselem from IPS data: 359 Palestinian minors held in June 2025.
US juveniles in residential placement fell 65% between 1997 and 2019 to 36,479; Black youth 41% of those in placement in 2019; the 2022 number was 75% below 2000, up about 10% from 2020.
Amnesty, 1 July 2026: 15 men remain at Guantanamo; nearly 800 held since January 2002; six never charged or tried (three neither charged nor approved for transfer; three approved for transfer).
TRAC: ICE detention peaked at 68,289 in early February 2026 (73.6% with no criminal conviction); 60,311 on 4 April 2026 (70.8% no conviction).
